events.why: The subgiant star swelled to fill its Roche lobe and began pouring gas onto its 1.50 solar mass companion. The mass ratio 2.00 is below the critical 4.00, so the flow is stable.
The donor has given away its whole envelope: its bare 0.32 solar mass core is left, a white dwarf from now.

references.text: Hurley, J. R., Tout, C. A. and Pols, O. R. 2002, MNRAS 329, 897: critical mass ratios for stable transfer (0.695 for low-mass main-sequence donors, 3 above about 0.7 solar masses as in BSE, 4 in the Hertzsprung gap, eq. 57 on the giant branch). arXiv:astro-ph/0201220
Webbink, R. F. 1984, ApJ 277, 355; de Kool, M. 1990, ApJ 358, 189: common-envelope energy budget, alpha = 1, lambda = 0.5
Jeans, J. H. 1924, Cosmogonic problems associated with a secular decrease of mass, MNRAS 85, 2: an orbit widens as a·M stays constant while the pair slowly loses mass.
Eggleton, P. P. 1983, Approximations to the radii of Roche lobes, ApJ 268, 368: r_L/a = 0.49 q^(2/3) / (0.6 q^(2/3) + ln(1 + q^(1/3))), good to 1 % for any mass ratio.

Hurley, J. R., Tout, C. A. and Pols, O. R. 2002, Evolution of binary stars and the effect of tides on binary populations, MNRAS 329, 897: overflow rate F(M) [ln(R/R_L)]³ M☉/yr with F = 3e-6 (min(M, 5))² (eq. 58), capped by the donor's thermal timescale τ_KH = 1.5e7 M (M − M_c) / (R L) yr in solar units (eq. 61).
Kelvin, Lord 1862 and Helmholtz, H. von 1856: a star's thermal timescale is the time its light takes to carry off its gravitational binding energy.

stand_ins: steps keep each star's radius within 0.02 and each transfer step within 0.01 of the envelope; rows every 0.02 change
the accretor keeps at most 10 times its own thermal rate, the rest leaving from beside it with its orbital angular momentum
a white dwarf, neutron star or black hole keeps none of the gas it is given (novae and X-ray binaries are BX4)
a donor stripped to its core is a white dwarf of that core from then (a helium star stage is left out)
a main-sequence star rebuilt at its new mass keeps its share of the main sequence; an accretor's share falls as the mass ratio (fresh fuel mixed into its core)
a pair acting as one body one level up trades no gas; a death is still the life line's slow mass loss (jumps and kicks are BX2)
ages in millions of years like F7's events, until the time scales design (TP1) converts both

events.why: The star swelled to 0.49 au and swallowed the planet orbiting at 0.48 au.

The giant star overflowed its Roche lobe faster than its 0.30 solar mass companion could take the gas (mass ratio 2.64, critical 0.69). The companion was engulfed; drag pulled the orbit in from 1.190 to 0.0579 au and the released energy blew the 0.36 solar mass envelope away, leaving the bare 0.43 solar mass core.
